title: reverseproxy: propagate TCP half-close on upgraded streams
body:
Fixes #8026.

## What

`handleUpgradeResponse` starts one copy goroutine per direction but returns as soon as the **first** one reports a result, and returning runs two unconditional deferred closes — the client connection and the backend connection. So a client that ends its send direction with a TCP half-close tears down the whole tunnel: the backend connection is reset mid-conversation and whatever it was about to send is never delivered.

This treats a clean EOF as the end of **one direction** rather than the end of the tunnel:

- when a copy finishes without error, the half-close is propagated to the destination with `CloseWrite` where the connection supports it, and the handler keeps waiting for the other direction so pending bytes can still drain;
- real copy errors, the stream timeout, and request cancellation / shutdown still tear down immediately;
- if the destination does **not** support `CloseWrite`, the peer cannot be told the direction ended, so the previous behavior is kept and the tunnel is torn down rather than held open until `StreamTimeout`. That keeps the change strictly additive — no configuration can start holding connections open that would not have been held open before.

Same class as [go.dev/issue/35892](https://go.dev/issue/35892), fixed in `net/http/httputil` in Go 1.25. Caddy has its own upgraded-stream copier, so the standard library fix does not reach this path — the binary I tested is built with Go 1.25.1 and still reproduces without this patch.

## Verification

Using the dependency-free reproduction from #8026 (a client whose only difference between runs is one `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` call), against the same origin and config:

**Before (v2.11.4, and `master` without this patch)**

```
CONTROL  keeps write side open -> 101 | payload=True  | client_end=payload | origin=['write1_ok', 'write2_ok(conn_alive)', 'recv_EOF']
TEST     shutdown(SHUT_WR)     -> 101 | payload=False | client_end=EOF     | origin=['write1_ok', 'write2_failed:EPIPE(conn_torn_down)', 'recv_err:ECONNRESET']
```

**After (this patch)**

```
CONTROL  keeps write side open -> 101 | payload=True  | client_end=payload | origin=['write1_ok', 'write2_ok(conn_alive)', 'recv_EOF']
TEST     shutdown(SHUT_WR)     -> 101 | payload=True  | client_end=payload | origin=['write1_ok', 'write2_ok(conn_alive)', 'recv_EOF']
```

3/3 runs each. All three symptoms clear: the client receives the payload, the origin connection stays usable instead of returning `EPIPE`, and the origin sees a graceful `EOF` instead of `ECONNRESET`. The control path is unchanged.

Also run:

- `go test ./modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/...` — pass
- `go test ./modules/caddyhttp/...` — pass, no regressions
- `go test -race -count=2 ./modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/` — pass
- `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` — clean

## Tests added

- `TestSwitchProtocolCopierHalfClose` — a clean EOF propagates CloseWrite when the destination
  supports it (reporting nil), reports `errCopyDone` when it does not, and reports the error when
  CloseWrite itself fails.
- `TestSwitchProtocolCopierErrorIsNotHalfClose` — a copy error is reported as-is and CloseWrite is
  not called, so the tunnel is still torn down immediately.
- `TestHandlerUpgradedStreamHalfClose` — an end-to-end test modelled on net/http/httputil's
  `TestReverseProxyWebSocketHalfTCP`: a backend that hijacks and hands back a `*net.TCPConn`, the
  handler in front of it, a client dialling it directly, and the four close-read / close-write
  combinations. Against the unfixed handler the two half-close cases fail and the two close-read
  cases pass, so it isolates exactly this behaviour.
- `TestSwitchProtocolCopierBufferSize` updated for the sentinel.

## Notes for review

Following review, this now mirrors `net/http/httputil`: a plain `chan error`, the `errCopyDone`
sentinel, and CloseWrite propagated inside the copier. The one deliberate difference is that the
wait is repeated inside the existing `select` rather than written as upstream's two-line form,
because `handleUpgradeResponse` also selects on the stream timeout and sizes the channel at 2 so
both goroutines can exit when it fires (#7418). The reasoning is in a comment beside the loop.

## Assistance Disclosure

An LLM (Claude) was used substantially here: it drafted the patch and the tests, and I directed, verified and am submitting the work. To be specific about the split, since the project asks for it:

- **AI-assisted:** the code in `streaming.go`, the three tests, the commit message and this description.
- **Mine:** the investigation and the decision to fix it this way; building this branch and running the reproduction and the test suites against it; the design call that a destination without `CloseWrite` must keep the old teardown behavior rather than hold the tunnel open until `StreamTimeout`.
- **Verified, not assumed:** every claim above is program output from this branch on my machine, not a description. The reproduction in #8026 was also executed against a real v2.11.4 binary before the issue was filed.

Per CONTRIBUTING, I have read and comprehend every line of this change and can explain it; it is a small, self-contained diff and I am happy to walk through any part of it in review. I'll sign the CLA.
